resources.title: A Field Study of Sediment Transport
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Studies in Computational Pragmatics (2024)

paragraphs: We study sediment transport across five monitoring stations using a hierarchical model.
Authors: Jonas Tanaka, Yusuf Bianchi, Rosa Castell, Noor Oduya. Published in Studies in Computational Pragmatics, 2024.
Table 2 reports the median latency for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report median latency measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2022 and 2024. A pilot survey in 2019 had put the regional median latency at 22.9 ms; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of sediment transport relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2021 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2024 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the median latency for each station in the 2024 campaign. The largest change relative to 2021 was observed at station N-26.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Thorvald et al. (2018). [2] Whitcombe and Ilunga (2020). [3] Tanaka et al. (2021).
